Name: Protein folding
Reference: Kubelka Hofrichter & Eaton (2004) Curr Opin Struct Biol 14:76 (BioNumbers 112314) — folding speed limit ~N/100 us for an N-residue single-domain protein; 0.35 us for N = 35. Upper bound of 1 s is not sourced

Name: DNA replication (single origin)
Reference: Fork speed ~1000 nt/s in E. coli: Rocha (2004) Microbiology 150:1609 (BioNumbers 110932); a 4.6 Mb chromosome copied by two forks from one origin takes ~2300 s. Lower bound is not sourced

Name: mRNA transcription
Reference: Elongation 42 nt/s (E. coli rRNA operons; BioNumbers 101904) to 71.6 nt/s (mammalian Pol II maximum; BioNumbers 100662): a 1 kb gene takes ~24 s and a 30 kb gene ~420 s; see data/references/bionumbers_subset.csv

Name: ATP synthesis (single molecule)
Reference: Rate >100 ATP per s so <=0.01 s per ATP (BioNumbers 111975); volume is the F1Fo synthase: 540-585 kDa (BioNumbers 111973) at an assumed protein density of 1.35 g/cm3 gives 6.6e-25 to 7.2e-25 m3; range is the half decade around it

Name: Enzyme catalytic cycle
Reference: Bar-Even et al. (2011) Biochemistry 50:4402 (BioNumbers 111411) — median kcat ~10 s-1 with ~60% of enzymes at 1-100 s-1; cycle time = 1/kcat for kcat 1 to 1e6 s-1

Name: Ribosome translation
Reference: Volume of the E. coli 70S ribosome 2680 nm3 (2.7e-24 m3): Gabashvili et al. (2000) Cell 100:537 (BioNumbers 100122); range is the decade around it. Time: 14.5 aa/s in E. coli (BioNumbers 100233) to 5 aa/s in human (BioNumbers 104598) gives 21-60 s for 300 residues and 600 s for 3000

Name: Virus assembly
Reference: Phage genome packaging ~5 min and eclipse period ~10-15 min: Purohit et al. (2005) Biophys J 88:851 (BioNumbers 111588). Volume V = (4/3) pi r^3 for capsid mean radii ~10-200 nm: Losdorfer Bozic et al. (2013) J Biol Phys 39:215 (BioNumbers 112740). The 1e4 s upper bound is not sourced

Name: Bacterial cell division
Reference: Within-range examples: Synechocystis PCC 6803 generation time 5.13 h (BioNumbers 111335) to 12 h (BioNumbers 111252); see data/references/bionumbers_subset.csv. The 20 min lower bound is not sourced here

Name: Mitochondrial fission/fusion
Reference: Fusion lasts tens of seconds to several minutes and each mitochondrion cycles about every 20 min: Mouli et al. (2009) Biophys J (PMC2711405). Volume 0.27 um3 for isolated rat liver mitochondria: Schwerzmann et al. (1986) J Cell Biol 102:97 (BioNumbers 107136). Upper volume bound (a fused network) is not sourced

Name: Calcium signaling wave
Reference: Fast calcium waves 10-30 um/s: Jaffe (2008) Phil Trans R Soc B (PMC2610120); crossing a 21 um cell takes 0.7-2.1 s. Cell volume 2425 um3 for HeLa (2.4e-15 m3): Zhao et al. (2008) NMR Biomed 21:159 (BioNumbers 103725). Bounds beyond these are not sourced

Name: Yeast cell cycle
Reference: Jorgensen et al. (2002) Science 297:395 (BioNumbers 100427) — median haploid S. cerevisiae volume 42 um3 (4.2e-17 m3); range brackets small daughters to large diploids

Name: White blood cell migration
Reference: Neutrophil speed 0.15 um/s in vitro: Vereycken et al. (1995) J Phys III 5:1469 (BioNumbers 106809); time is path/speed for 0.1-5 mm paths. Cell volume 320 +/- 37 fL resting and 375 +/- 56 fL activated: Rosengren et al. (1994) Am J Physiol 267:C1623 (BioNumbers 108241)

Name: Neuron action potential
Reference: Duration about 1 ms (Wikipedia: Action potential; no primary source fetched). Soma volume 12260 um3 (1.2e-14 m3) in guinea pig: Edstrom (1957) J Comp Neurol 107:295 (BioNumbers 112112)

Name: Red blood cell lifespan
Reference: Lifespan ~120 days: Vander et al. (2001) Human Physiology p. 377 (BioNumbers 101706). Volume 97 um3 (9.7e-17 m3): Frank et al. (1997) J Appl Physiol 82:2036 (BioNumbers 101711) which also notes ~90 fL

Name: Liver cell turnover
Reference: Plettenberg et al. (2008) Pflugers Arch 455:1089 (BioNumbers 104616) — rat hepatocyte ~7000 um3 (7e-15 m3); range is V = (pi/6) d^3 for d = 20-30 um

Name: Skin cell turnover (epidermis)
Reference: Epidermal turnover 26-27 days: Weinstein & Van Scott (1965) J Invest Dermatol 45:257 (BioNumbers 109215). The 40 day upper bound and the volume range are not sourced

Name: Heartbeat (single beat)
Reference: Standard cardiac physiology; stroke volume ~70 mL

Name: Human breath cycle
Reference: Resting rate 12-15 breaths per min (4-5 s): Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology via Wikipedia: Respiratory rate. Tidal volume ~0.5 L and total lung capacity ~6 L: StatPearls NBK482502 and NBK541029

Name: Butterfly wing beat
Reference: Dudley J Exp Biol 150:37-53 — 37 Panamanian butterfly species: wingbeat 5.9-23.0 Hz (mean 11 Hz) and body mass 17.4-1841 mg; V = m / 1000 kg m-3

Name: Housefly lifespan
Reference: UF/IFAS EDIS IN205 — adults usually live 15-25 days and up to two months. Volume range is not sourced

Name: Mayfly adult lifespan
Reference: Britannica: mayfly — winged stage may last only a few hours; Hexagenia up to two days (BioKIDS Univ. of Michigan). Volume range is not sourced

Name: E. coli doubling
Reference: Phillips Kondev & Theriot (2009) Physical Biology of the Cell p. 26 (BioNumbers 101788) — rule-of-thumb E. coli volume 1 um3 (1e-18 m3); volume varies with medium and growth rate (Kubitschek & Friske 1986 J Bacteriol 168:1466) so range is +/- half a decade

Name: Mouse lifespan
Reference: Median lifespan 251-964 days across 31 inbred strains: Yuan et al. (2009) Aging Cell 8:277. C57BL/6J at 20 weeks 24.7 g (female) to 33.6 g (male): Jackson Laboratory body weight chart 000664; V = m / 1000 kg m-3. Lower volume bound is not sourced

Name: Domestic cat lifespan
Reference: Lifespan 13-20 yr (Wikipedia: Aging in cats) and ~14 yr in captivity; mass 4.1-5.4 kg: Animal Diversity Web Felis catus; AnAge adult weight 3.9 kg; V = m / 1000 kg m-3

Name: Dog lifespan
Reference: Animal Diversity Web Canis lupus familiaris — well-cared-for dogs live 12 years or more; mass <1 to 70 kg; V = m / 1000 kg m-3. Lifespan bounds are not sourced

Name: Human lifespan
Reference: WHO life expectancy tables; body volume ~0.07 m³

Name: Blue whale lifespan
Reference: Sears & Perrin (2009) Blue whale Balaenoptera musculus; pp. 120-124 in Encyclopedia of Marine Mammals 2nd ed. (Academic Press)

Name: Giant tortoise lifespan
Reference: Jaffe Slater & Alfaro (2011) Biology Letters doi:10.1098/rsbl.2010.1084; Chiari et al. (2017) — adult Chelonoidis niger commonly >100 kg to ~400 kg; V = m / 1000 kg m-3

Name: Bowhead whale lifespan
Reference: Over 200 yr: George et al. (1999) Can J Zool 77:571 as cited by North Slope Borough Wildlife Management; oldest estimate 211 yr (AnAge). Mass up to 200000 lb (91 t): NOAA Fisheries; V = m / 1000 kg m-3

Name: Greenland shark lifespan
Reference: Age 272-512 yr: Nielsen et al. (2016) Science 353(6300):702-704. Volume for large adults (the oldest animals are the largest): 775 kg IGFA record to 1023 kg largest confirmed specimen; V = m / 1000 kg m-3

Name: Sunflower lifespan
Reference: SDSU Extension P-00205-02 — sunflower hybrids mature in 80 to 100 days. Volume range is not sourced

Name: Oak tree lifespan
Reference: USDA Forest Service Silvics: white oak — often 24-30 m tall and 0.91-1.22 m in diameter; individuals 46 m tall 2.44 m in diameter and 600 years old recorded. Volume is a trunk cylinder pi r^2 h (16-35 m3 typical; 215 m3 record) and overstates a tapering trunk. The 100 yr lower bound is not sourced

Name: Giant sequoia lifespan
Reference: Stephenson (2000) USGS; NPS Sequoia & Kings Canyon — General Sherman is the largest tree at 52508 ft3 (1487 m3) trunk volume

Name: Bristlecone pine lifespan
Reference: Oldest living trees 4847 and 5065 yr: NPS Great Basin National Park. Trees 6-12 m tall with trunks 0.3-0.8 m in diameter: NPS Bryce Canyon; volume is a trunk cylinder pi r^2 h

Name: Mushroom fruiting body
Reference: Shiitake pins appear 3-5 days and are harvested 7-10 days after shocking: Ohio State Extension F-0042. Agaricus bisporus cap 2.5-14 cm and stem 2-7 cm x 1-2.5 cm: MushroomExpert.com; volume from a stem cylinder plus hemispherical cap is 6e-6 to 7.5e-4 m3

Name: Mycelial network (forest floor)
Reference: Oregon Armillaria ostoyae: estimated 1900-8650 yr old and 7567-35000 tons over 2200 acres: USDA Forest Service (usda.gov blog). Biomass volume 7e3 to 3e4 m3 at 1000 kg m-3; occupied soil volume would be larger and is not sourced

Name: Pando aspen clone lifespan
Reference: Extent: Mock et al. (2008) Mol Ecol; DeWoody et al. (2008); 43 ha × ~2m root depth. Age 16000-80000 yr: Pineau et al. (2024) bioRxiv preprint (Mosaic of somatic mutations in Earth's oldest living organism Pando)

Name: Tide pool cycle
Reference: NOAA National Ocean Service tides tutorial — high tides occur 12 hours and 25 minutes apart (44700 s). Pool volume is not sourced

Name: Forest fire
Reference: Upper time bound: August Complex 2020 active for 87 days (CAL FIRE). Mean US wildfire in 2025 was 66 acres (NICC annual report). Lower time bound and the canopy height behind the volume are not sourced

Name: Coral reef growth
Reference: NOAA National Ocean Service corals tutorial — it can take up to 10000 years for a coral reef to form. Holocene reef accretion 0.38-4.85 m per 1000 yr: USGS St. Petersburg Coastal and Marine Science Center. Volume range is not sourced

Name: Kelp forest cycle
Reference: Giant kelp lives six to eight years on average: SIMoN species database; seven years at most: NASA Earth Observatory. Forests grow in 5-30 m of water; forest area and so volume are not sourced

Name: Prairie grassland cycle
Reference: USDA Forest Service FEIS — historical fire return intervals of 1 to 35 years in plains grassland and prairie. Volume example: Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve 10894 acres x 1.2-2.1 m grass height = 5e7 to 9e7 m3 (NPS)

Name: Seasonal algal bloom
Reference: Spring bloom lasts 39-46 days in most North and Norwegian Sea sub-regions and up to 58 days in one (5.01e6 s): Silva et al. (2021) Front Mar Sci doi:10.3389/fmars.2021.746327; blooms last several weeks (NASA Earth Observatory). Volume range is not sourced

Name: River delta formation
Reference: USGS Open-File Report 98-36 — Mississippi delta complexes from 6-8 ka to the present with each lasting ~1000-2300 yr; deltaic plain 29785 km2. Holocene section up to 60 m thick (USGS) gives an upper bound of 1.8e12 m3

Name: Soil formation (1 cm topsoil)
Reference: USDA NRCS Illinois — it takes hundreds to thousands of years to build an inch of topsoil; Soil Science Society of America — 500 years to thousands per inch. Range is 100 yr per inch (39 yr per cm) to 1000 yr per cm. Volume depends on the plot area chosen

Name: Raindrop fall
Reference: Villermaux & Bossa (2009) Nat Phys 5:697 — drops break up above ~5-6 mm diameter; V = (pi/6) d^3 for d = 0.6-6 mm

Name: Thunderstorm cell
Reference: Single cell lifetime 30-60 min: NWS Spotter Guide; 20-30 min: AMS Glossary of Meteorology. Depth 12-18 km (NWS). A single-cell diameter was not found so the volume range is not sourced

Name: Tornado
Reference: NOAA Tornado FAQ — tornadoes last from several seconds to more than an hour and most last less than 10 minutes; widest path 2.6 miles (El Reno 2013). Funnel height and so the volume range are not sourced

Name: Hurricane lifetime
Reference: Merrill (1984) Mon Wea Rev 112:1408 — radius of outermost closed isobar from under 2 deg lat (r ~100 km) to 8 deg lat (r ~890 km); V = pi r^2 h over a 10-16 km tropical troposphere

Name: Monsoon season
Reference: India Meteorological Department — onset over Kerala around 1 June and withdrawal around 15 October (136 days). Volume: area of India 3.29e6 km2 x 18 km tropical troposphere = 5.9e16 m3 (areas and depth from Wikipedia)

Name: El Niño event
Reference: NOAA National Ocean Service — episodes typically last nine to 12 months but can sometimes last for years. Volume range is not sourced

Name: Ice age cycle (Milankovitch)
Reference: Charette & Smith (2010) Oceanography 23:112 — ocean 1.335e18 m3; atmosphere to 100 km = 5.1e14 m2 x 1e5 m = 5.1e19 m3. Bracket is a framing choice: which reservoir a glacial cycle 'occupies' is not well defined

Name: Surface wave
Reference: Hong Kong Observatory — ocean gravity waves have periods from 1 to 30 seconds. Volume depends on the crest length chosen and is not sourced

Name: Tidal cycle
Reference: NOAA National Ocean Service — high tides occur 12 hours and 25 minutes apart (44700 s). Volume range is not sourced

Name: Ocean eddy (mesoscale)
Reference: Chelton et al. (2011) Prog Oceanogr 91:167 — radii 25-150 km; V = pi r^2 h over a 300-2000 m thermocline

Name: Thermohaline circulation (full loop)
Reference: NOAA National Ocean Service — about 1000 years for a parcel of water to complete the global conveyor belt; ocean volume 1335000000 km3. The 2000 yr upper bound and the lower volume bound are not sourced

Name: Tsunami propagation
Reference: NOAA JetStream — Aleutians to Hawaii in about five hours; tsunamis can cross entire oceans in less than a day. Volume depends on the crest length chosen and is not sourced

Name: Computer transistor switch
Reference: Inverter delay 13.9 ps at 1 V: 2007 Symposium on VLSI Technology paper 7A-1. Upper time bound and the volume range are not sourced

Name: LED light pulse
Reference: Rise time 2.4 ns and fall time 1.1 ns for a resonant-cavity LED: Schubert Light-Emitting Diodes ch. 24. Chip 980 x 980 x 170 um (1.6e-10 m3): Cree EZ1000 data sheet

Name: Microchip (processor die)
Reference: Die area 146-217 mm2 (Pentium 4; Tom's Hardware) x 775 um wafer thickness (Wikipedia) = 1.1e-7 to 1.7e-7 m3. Useful lifetime 10 years at 105 C: Texas Instruments SPRABX4

Name: Smartphone
Reference: iPhone 16 is 71.6 x 147.6 x 7.80 mm (8.2e-5 m3): Apple technical specifications. Average US replacement cycle 33 months: Strategy Analytics 2019 via Mobile World Live

Name: A book (physical object)
Reference: Library of Congress — acidic paper becomes brittle in fifty to a hundred years; deacidified paper stays usable for several centuries. Hardcover 6 x 9 in; thickness and so volume are not sourced

Name: A house
Reference: US Census Bureau 2025 — median completed single-family home 2142 ft2 (199 m2); x an assumed 2.44 m ceiling = 485 m3. Service life is not sourced

Name: Skyscraper lifespan
Reference: Empire State Building volume 37 million ft3 (1.05e6 m3): official fact sheet. Lifespan is not sourced

Name: Highway bridge
Reference: Design life 75 years: AASHTO LRFD definition as quoted in a WSDOT bridge seminar; 50-75 years: FHWA-HRT-04-098. Volume range is not sourced

Name: Hoover Dam
Reference: US Bureau of Reclamation Hoover Dam FAQ — concrete: 3.25 million yd3 in the dam (2.48e6 m3); 4.36 million yd3 with powerplant and appurtenant works (3.33e6 m3)

Name: Panama Canal
Reference: Panama Canal Authority — about 268000000 cubic yards excavated in total (2.05e8 m3); opened 15 August 1914. Upper time bound is not sourced

Name: Mining operation (open pit)
Reference: Bingham Canyon: 4 km across and 1.2 km deep (Guinness World Records); in production since 1906 with mine life to 2027. Upper volume is an inverted cone (1/3) pi r^2 h = 5.0e9 m3. Lower bounds are not sourced

Name: Oil reservoir extraction
Reference: Prudhoe Bay: 25 billion barrels originally in place and 13.5 billion expected lifetime production (2.1e9 to 4.0e9 m3 of oil): US EIA. Ghawar on stream since 1951 with over 65 billion barrels produced (Wikipedia). Lower bounds are not sourced

Name: Landfill decomposition
Reference: US EPA landfill gas model — first-order decay constants 0.04 to 0.12 per year; time to 99 percent decay is 4.6/k = 38-115 yr. Volume range is not sourced

Name: Nuclear waste half-life (Pu-239)
Reference: US NRC Fact Sheet on Plutonium — Pu-239 has a half-life of 24000 years. The volume range has no defined referent

Name: Great Wall of China
Reference: Ming wall masonry estimate; V = length x width x height: 6259 km built wall x 5 m x 6 m = 1.9e8 m3 to 8850 km x 6.5 m x 7.8 m = 4.5e8 m3. Cross-section applied uniformly along the wall

Name: International Space Station (service life)
Reference: NASA Space Station Facts and Figures — pressurized volume 35491 ft3 (1005 m3); time is service life (15-30 yr) not the ~5400 s orbital period

Name: A pond
Reference: USDA NRCS Agriculture Handbook 590 — example pond of 3.2 acres holds 16 acre-feet (2.0e4 m3). Constructed ponds are designed for a 50-year lifespan (Iowa Nutrient Research Center). Lower bounds are not sourced

Name: A lake (e.g. Tahoe)
Reference: Lake Tahoe: 192 mi2 x 1000 ft mean depth = 1.5e11 m3 (USGS WRIR 02-4030). Modern lake began to form about 2 million years ago (EARTH Magazine AGI). Lower time bound is not sourced

Name: San Francisco Bay
Reference: Volume 6.66e9 m3 at mean lower low water: Chin & Clifton (1990) USGS Open-File Report 90-665 citing Conomos (1979). The sea entered the Golden Gate 10000-11000 years ago: USGS Professional Paper 1014. Upper time bound is not sourced

Name: Grand Canyon formation
Reference: NPS Grand Canyon park statistics — volume 5.45 trillion cubic yards (4.17e12 m3)

Name: France (area × avg elevation)
Reference: CIA World Factbook (openfactbook.org mirror) — metropolitan France 551500 km2 and mean elevation 375 m; V = area x mean elevation = 2.07e14 m3. The time value is not sourced

Name: Mediterranean Sea
Reference: Wikipedia: Mediterranean Sea — volume 3750000 km3 (area 2500000 km2 x mean depth 1500 m); Zanclean reflooding 5.33 million years ago. No primary source fetched

Name: Amazon rainforest
Reference: Area 5.5e6 to 6.0e6 km2 (Britannica) x mean canopy height ~22 m (arXiv:2501.10600) = 1.2e14 to 1.3e14 m3. The time range is not sourced; the forest itself is at least 55 million years old

Name: Pacific Ocean
Reference: Volume: NOAA ETOPO1 area 161760000 km2 x mean depth 4080 m = 6.6e17 m3; Wikipedia gives 7.1e17. Oldest in situ Pacific crust ~160 Ma: Floyd Castillo & Pringle (1991) Terra Nova; ~180 Ma per Wikipedia

Name: Volcanic eruption (single event)
Reference: Mount St. Helens 1980: 9 hours of vigorous eruption and 1.3 km3 of ash (USGS). Pinatubo 1991: over 10 km3 (Wikipedia). Upper time bound is not sourced

Name: Earthquake rupture
Reference: USGS: 2004 Sumatra M9.0 — rupture lasted 3 to 4 minutes over 1200-1300 km length and >100 km width with up to 20 m slip; V = length x width x slip = 2.6e12 m3. Rupture speed ~2 km/s (USGS). Lower bounds are not sourced

Name: Mountain building (orogeny)
Reference: USGS This Dynamic Earth — India met Asia 40 to 50 million years ago and the Himalayas stretch 2900 km. Volume ~3e15 m3 for 2400 km x 250 km x an assumed 5 km mean relief. Lower time bound is not sourced

Name: Continental drift (1 cm/yr)
Reference: USGS This Dynamic Earth — the Atlantic opened over the past 100 to 200 million years; spreading rates run from under 2.5 to over 15 cm/yr so the 1 cm/yr in the name is slower than any quoted rate. Volume range is not sourced

Name: Continental crust formation
Reference: Wikipedia: Continental crust — about 7 billion km3 of continental crust; oldest intact fragment the Acasta Gneiss at 4.01 Ga. No primary source fetched

Name: Pangaea assembly/breakup
Reference: Britannica: Pangea — fully assembled 299 to 273 million years ago and began to break apart about 200 million years ago; time is the 73-99 Myr between. Volume range is not sourced

Name: Stalactite growth (1 m)
Reference: Average growth ~0.1 mm per year (EBSCO Research Starters) to 0.13 mm per year (Wikipedia: Stalactite) gives 7700-10000 yr per metre; fastest 3 mm per year gives 330 yr. Volume range is not sourced

Name: Earth's rotation (1 day)
Reference: Mean solar day 86400 s by definition. Volume 1.08e21 m3: sphere of the IAU nominal equatorial radius 6378.1 km is 1.087e21 m3 and the polar flattening removes ~0.3 percent

Name: Earth's orbit (1 year)
Reference: One year is 3.156e7 s. Volume is the sphere enclosed by the orbit: V = (4/3) pi r^3 with r = 1 au (1.496e11 m) = 1.41e34 m3

Name: Moon formation
Reference: Hours: Kegerreis et al. (2022) ApJ Letters arXiv:2210.01814 (satellite placed in orbit immediately). Up to ~1 yr: Ida Canup & Stewart (1997) Nature 25 Sept 1997 (accretion from the impact disk in a year or less). Volume is the present Moon

Name: Earth's age
Reference: USGS Geologic Time: Age of the Earth — 4.54 billion years with an uncertainty of less than 1 percent (1.43e17 s). Volume is the present Earth

Name: Sun's main sequence lifetime
Reference: NASA Sun facts — the Sun is 4.5 billion years old and a little less than halfway through its lifetime with about 5 billion years left (~10 Gyr = 3.2e17 s). Volume 1.41e27 m3 from the IAU nominal solar radius; 1.3 million Earths
